title: Spatial OS
tagline: A window manager for spatial computing environments
description: Designed and prototyped a spatial operating system concept for XR headsets, featuring gesture-driven window management, persistent application state, and multi-modal input.

slides.title: The Problem
slides.content: Current XR operating systems replicate 2D desktop metaphors in 3D space — floating flat panels, clunky pinch-to-click, no persistent spatial memory. This ignores the spatial nature of the medium and limits productivity in mixed reality.

slides.title: Why It Matters
slides.content: XR is the next computing platform, but it won't replace desktops until the UX is fundamentally better — not just a 2D UI floating in space. Spatial OS explores what a native spatial computing paradigm looks like: windows as physical objects, gestures as verbs, and space as persistent state.

slides.title: The Solution
slides.content: Built a prototype using Three.js and WebXR that treats application windows as physics-enabled 3D objects. Windows can be stacked, thrown, pinned to real-world surfaces, and grouped into spatial workspaces. Input combines hand tracking, eye gaze, and voice commands in a layered interaction model.

slides.title: Technical Architecture
slides.content: The system uses a component-entity architecture with a spatial physics engine (Cannon.js) for window physics. A spatial anchor system maps digital content to real-world surfaces using WebXR anchors. The input layer processes hand tracking, eye gaze (WebGazer), and voice (Web Speech API) through a priority-weighted fusion engine.

media.alt: Demo of Spatial OS gesture interactions

slides.title: Results & Impact
slides.content: User testing showed 40% faster task completion for multi-window workflows compared to current XR OS UX patterns. The spatial persistence model was presented at a XR conference and influenced design discussions at two hardware companies.

slides.title: Learnings
slides.content: Eye gaze as primary input is more natural but less precise than hand tracking — next version will use a hybrid model. Physics-based windows need damping to avoid nausea. I'd also implement a spatial bookmarking system for saving and restoring workspace layouts.
